title: Oil Slide and Energy Stocks
summary: Gotrade News - Oil prices suffered a steep weekly slide, and US energy stocks fell with them. According to CNBC , Brent crude futures settled at $98.32 a

Diamondback's slide began on Monday, November 2, the day the company published its quarterly[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) , when the stock fell 5.8%. It dropped another 4.9% on Wednesday as crude tumbled, according to the same StockAnalysis data.


## Diamondback Q3: 525,000 Barrels a Day and a 7.3% Dividend Increase


According to Diamondback's[third-quarter release filed with the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001539838/000153983826000180/diamondbackex991-11x2x26.htm) , the company averaged 525,000 barrels of oil per day, or 1.034 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, in the third quarter of 2026. Adjusted earnings came in at $5.86 per diluted share. The company generated $2.6 billion of operating cash flow and $2.1 billion of free cash flow on $1.0 billion of capital spending. Its realized oil price was $87.30 a barrel, down from $96.82 in the second quarter but up from $64.60 a year earlier.


The board raised the quarterly base dividend 7.3% to $1.18 per share, or $4.72 annualized, which the company said equals an annualized[dividend yield](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/dividend-yield-meaning-and-formula/) of about 2.2% based on its October 30 closing price. Diamondback also repurchased 1,348,209 shares for about $251 million in the quarter, bringing its total return of capital to $582 million.


The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance to about 524,000 barrels of oil per day, from 522,000 or more, and lifted its capital budget range to $3.95 billion to $4.00 billion. Even after the week's slide, WTI's Friday settlement of $90.83 sat above the $87.30 a barrel Diamondback realized in the third quarter.


## Seeking Alpha View: Diamondback Shares Imply $67 Oil


In an analysis published on[Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4964873-diamondback-energy-stock-is-pricing-in-67bbl-oil-i-see-40-percent-plus-upside) on November 8, contributor Elliott Gue argued that Diamondback's share price implies oil of about $67 a barrel, pointing to the company's low production costs, capital efficiency, low reinvestment rate and extended drilling inventory. That is the author's own valuation view, built on a discounted cash flow model that assumes conservative production growth and higher cash taxes.


## Rapidan Sees 80% Odds of Renewed Iran Fighting


Not every analyst expects lower crude to last. Per CNBC, Rapidan Energy Group founder and president Bob McNally sees an 80% probability of military fighting resuming and expects both benchmarks could climb back above $100 a barrel.


> Bob McNally, Rapidan Energy Group, told CNBC: "as long as that core difference in that deal space is absent, the escalation dynamic remains in place."


CNBC reported that investors are assessing whether the end of the midterm elections could lead to renewed US action against Iran, potentially threatening Middle East oil supplies.
